external_entities.name: colleague
external_entities.description: A colleague who signs in through the identity broker and uses applications.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are, including their own devices at home.
external_entities.notes: The text does not state whether colleagues are asked for a second factor.

external_entities.name: franchise colleague
external_entities.description: A colleague from a franchise store who is vouched for by the franchise's identity provider.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Franchise colleagues do not have staff accounts with us; their own identity provider vouches for them
external_entities.notes: The text does not state which colleagues the provider is allowed to vouch for.

external_entities.name: colleague's own device
external_entities.description: A device used by a colleague to sign in from home.
external_entities.source_excerpt: including their own devices at home

external_entities.name: HR system
external_entities.description: The system that supplies overnight changes to colleague and group membership data.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Group membership is not maintained there by hand — it comes from the HR system overnight.

external_entities.name: franchise identity provider
external_entities.description: The identity provider used by franchise colleagues to vouch for their identities.
external_entities.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them
external_entities.notes: The text does not state which party operates the provider or where it runs.

external_entities.name: franchise store
external_entities.description: A franchise store whose colleagues are allowed to use the sign-in system.
external_entities.source_excerpt: We also let the franchise stores in.

processes.name: identity broker
processes.description: Signs colleagues in, issues tokens, validates federated sign-in, supplies public signing keys, and records sign-ins.
processes.source_excerpt: Everything colleagues use signs them in through one identity broker.
processes.notes: The text does not state whether colleagues are asked for a second factor.

processes.name: application
processes.description: An application that accepts the broker's token and decides what a colleague may do from its groups.
processes.source_excerpt: Every application takes that token and decides what the colleague may do from the groups in it.

processes.name: store admin console
processes.description: An application that allows a holder of a store-manager token to change prices and void transactions.
processes.source_excerpt: If the token has the store-manager group in it, the console lets the holder change prices and void transactions.
processes.notes: The console does not check which store the colleague belongs to, so a store-manager token works against every store.

data_stores.name: key store
data_stores.description: A store holding the signing key used by the identity broker for tokens.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.

data_stores.name: directory
data_stores.description: The identity broker's store of colleagues and their group memberships.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has written down whether the directory is encrypted where it sits.

data_stores.name: audit log
data_stores.description: A log to which the identity broker writes sign-ins.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has written down what the log records, whether it covers the franchise route, or whether it is encrypted where it sits.

data_flows.name: sign-in
data_flows.description: A colleague signs in to the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are, including their own devices at home.

data_flows.name: issue token
data_flows.description: The identity broker issues a token to a signed-in colleague.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Once the broker has signed a colleague in it issues them a token.
data_flows.notes: The token carries the colleague's staff id and a list of the groups they are in.
data_flows.data_description: Token containing staff id and group membership

data_flows.name: present token
data_flows.description: A colleague presents the broker-issued token to an application.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every application takes that token and decides what the colleague may do from the groups in it.
data_flows.data_description: Broker-issued token containing staff id and group membership

data_flows.name: change prices
data_flows.description: A colleague uses the store admin console to change prices or void transactions.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the console lets the holder change prices and void transactions.
data_flows.notes: The console does not check which store the colleague belongs to.

data_flows.name: fetch public key
data_flows.description: The store admin console fetches the public half of the broker's signing key.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Applications fetch the public half from the broker to check the signature.

data_flows.name: store signing key
data_flows.description: The identity broker keeps its signing key in the key store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.

data_flows.name: update membership
data_flows.description: The identity broker updates its directory with colleague and group membership changes.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker pulls the changes once a night
data_flows.notes: The same overnight change process is how leavers stop being colleagues.

data_flows.name: pull changes
data_flows.description: The identity broker pulls colleague and group membership changes from the HR system overnight.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker pulls the changes once a night

data_flows.name: vouch for colleague
data_flows.description: The franchise identity provider vouches for a franchise colleague and the broker accepts that as sign-in.
data_flows.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them and the broker takes that as a sign-in.
data_flows.notes: The text does not state which colleagues the provider is allowed to vouch for.

data_flows.name: write sign-ins
data_flows.description: The identity broker writes sign-in events to the audit log.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_flows.notes: The text does not state whether the log covers the franchise route.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network on which the identity broker and store admin console run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The broker runs on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: colleague home
trust_boundaries.description: The home environment containing colleagues' own devices.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: including their own devices at home

assumptions.assumption: The identity broker is internal because the text says it runs on the corporate network.
assumptions.basis: The source states: "The broker runs on the corporate network."

assumptions.assumption: The store admin console is internal because the text says it runs on the corporate network.
assumptions.basis: The source states: "It also runs on the corporate network."

assumptions.assumption: The key store's data classification is confidential because it holds a signing key.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the key store holds the signing key used to sign tokens.

assumptions.assumption: The directory's data classification is confidential because it holds colleagues and their group memberships.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the directory keeps colleagues and the groups they are in.

assumptions.assumption: The audit log's data classification is confidential because it holds sign-in events associated with colleagues.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the broker writes sign-ins to the audit log.
